Miguel (Acme Corp): Hey team — running into a weird failure on our embeddings ingestion after yesterday's traffic spike. Calls to /v1/embeddings return vectors but our vector DB throws: "Embedding dimension mismatch: expected 1536 got 768". Its intermittent (~3-5% of requests) and coincides with p95 latency spikes.
Jules (Support): thanks — can you share the raw response body + region header you set? Also any x-rw-request-id?
Miguel (Acme Corp): Sample curl we use: 
```
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \ 
  -H \"Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY\" \ 
  -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" \ 
  -H \"X-Redwood-Region: eu-west-1\" \ 
  -d '{\"model\":\"embed-003\",\"input\":\"foo\"}'
```
When the error happens the client logs show response: `{ "data":[{"embedding":[..len=768..], "model":"embed-003-legacy","object":"embedding"}] }` and header `x-rw-request-id: rw_req_20260315_9c2f`.
Ava (Infra): copying routing logs for that request id...
Leo (SRE): pulled it: `rw_req_20260315_9c2f => routed_region=us-east-1 target_model=embed-003-legacy node=gpu-node-27 status=200 latency_ms=420`. Note routed_region != requested.
Kai (Eng Runtime): that explains dims — embed-003 is 1536, embed-003-legacy 768. Two main culprits: (1) cross-region spillover to a legacy pool; (2) batching/multiplexing bug that mixed models in a batch so a legacy worker handled some samples.
Jules (Support): why would routing cross regions? We should only fallback to compatible variants, right?
Ava (Infra): correct nominally. We have smart routing that can overflow when local capacity is exhausted or if startup latency (cold start) would violate SLOs. In this case eu-west autoscaler had reduced min instances during a lull; on sudden surge cold starts triggered and routing spilled to other regions. Worse, our compatibility matrix mistakenly listed embed-003-legacy as compatible with embed-003 so fallback returned mismatched dims.
Miguel (Acme Corp): Ugh. Can we mitigate quickly? This is breaking our pipeline.
Kai (Eng Runtime): immediate mitigations you can apply client-side: (A) pin the exact model version e.g. `model=embed-003@2026-02-01` to avoid variant fallback; (B) set `X-Redwood-Require-Region: true` to force failure (421) instead of cross-region fallback; (C) temporarily disable cross-model batching (`batching:false` or `max_batch_size:1`) to avoid mixed-model batches. Any of these should prevent 768-dim responses.
Jules (Support): Miguel, can you try pin + require-region and report?
Miguel (Acme Corp): applying `model=embed-003@2026-02-01` + `X-Redwood-Require-Region: true` now. Running a quick 1k request smoke. So far 0/1000 mismatches, p95 stable. Will watch 30m.
Ava (Infra): root cause summary from infra side: (1) eu-west autoscaler min dropped to 0 for some ephemeral pools; (2) sudden traffic caused cold starts and routing spilled to us-east; (3) an incorrect compatibility table entry allowed a legacy 768-dim variant as a fallback. Immediate actions: bump autoscaler min for embedding pools, add prewarm policy, and patch compatibility matrix to remove incorrect entry.
Kai (Eng Runtime): also found a missing validation path — runtime currently doesn't verify returned embedding dimensionality vs requested model before sending to client. I'll open a hotfix to validate dims and fail fast if mismatch. Ticket RUNTIME-1198 opened.
Leo (SRE): spun up 4 warm workers in eu-west (gpu-node-42..45) and adjusted autoscaler min to avoid scale-to-zero on popular embedding pools. ETA ~30m, monitoring.
deploy-bot: deploy started: infra/2026-03-15/prewarm-eu-west -> success in 32s
Miguel (Acme Corp): Confirming no mismatches 30m after mitigations. Thanks. Wed like a short postmortem + recommended client config for production safety. Also curious about billing impact — this caused failed ingests.
Jules (Support): noted. Draft customer note: "Intermittent embedding dimension mismatch caused by cross-region fallback to an older model variant during eu-west capacity shortage. Workaround: pin model version, set X-Redwood-Require-Region=true, and disable cross-model batching for ingest jobs. We're rolling infra and runtime fixes and will follow up with a postmortem and any billing adjustments as needed." Miguel — want me to send?
Miguel (Acme Corp): Please send. Include the recommended client flags.
Kai (Eng Runtime): opened PR: https://git.redwood.ai/r/runtime/pulls/834 (validate dims on return). Also RUNTIME-1199: preflight compatibility checks during routing.
Ava (Infra): INFRA-442: adjust autoscaler min eu-west; INFRA-443: prewarm policy for embedding pools. Rolling changes now, will update when complete.
Leo (SRE): eu-west warm workers online, traffic migrating back. Metrics look good.
Jules (Support): sending the customer message and creating a short internal postmortem doc. Action owners: Kai (runtime hotfix), Ava (infra prewarm/autoscaler), Jules (customer comms + postmortem). Will reopen if regressions occur. :wave:
